newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen rise with JGB surge, tone firm.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen rise with JGB surge, tone firm.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures broke above long-standing resistance levels on Thursday in line with sharp rises in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.

Dealers said the market looked well supported after U.S. Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony removed fears of a near-term credit tightening, easing potential pressure on Japan to raise rates.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly economic report indicating capital spending was unlikely to gather significant momentum for the time being reinforced the market perception of continued weaknesses in the economy.
The lead March Euroyen stood at its day high of 99.10 at 1115 GMT against an IMM close at 99.06 on volume of 15,715 lots.
A trader at a European futures house said locals triggered stop-loss buy orders, pushing the contract convincingly above 99.06, which had proved a stubborn barrier in recent months.
He said the contract would now be well supported at that level but was likely to face immediate resistance at 99.10.
September JGBs ended at 125.84 against a previous 125.55.
Eurodollar futures ended steady as players heaved a sigh of relief after the second part of Greenspan's testimony.
December Eurodollars finished unchanged against an IMM close at 94.135.
The dealer said the recent rally in U.S. treasuries looked overdone and the market could give up some of its gains.
